From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Checkout spike + errors after 'v3.2-int8' quant profile

Dylan / Evan — quick triage here from runtime side. Initial findings:

- Timeline matches: v3.2-int8 profile was deployed to Brightlane's dedicated pool at 12:37 PST.
- Symptom set: p95 latency + 5xx increase correlated with GPU decode stalls and memory-pressure-driven small OOMs in the warmup phase for longer sequences.
- Root cause hypothesis: the v3.2-int8 kernels expose a rare path in attention rematerialization for sequences >512 tokens — we didn't hit this in synthetic testing because Brightlane's checkout payloads sometimes include long product descriptions and user prompts concatenated with metadata. The quant path has tighter memory packing that increases tail latency when KV cache growth is uneven.

Immediate recommendation: rollback to v3.1-fp16 profile for Brightlane's production pool. This is a config toggle (no model swap) and will take approximately 8-12 minutes end-to-end, including canary and progressive rollout back to 100%.

Medium-term: produce a new v3.2-int8 patch that:
- avoids the specific rematerialization kernel for sequences >512, or
- introduces an adaptive decode memory cap for high-variance workloads.

I've attached a short profiling dump (profiling_report.zip) and sample stack traces. I'll join the bridge at 13:50.

—Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Runtime
